title: [V1][P/D] An native implementation of xPyD based on P2P NCCL (#18242)

experiments.name: intertoken_latency_p99
experiments.workload: Scenario 2 (1K input, 200 output tokens, E2E P99 latency ~4s): 1P1D on 2xA800 vs single-instance vLLM on 1xA800, Qwen model, random-input-len 1024 / random-output-len 1024 serving benchmark measuring ITL (P99).
experiments.note: diff adds the P2P NCCL xPyD KV-transfer connector (p2p_nccl_connector.py, p2p_nccl_engine.py, tensor_memory_pool.py) that disaggregates prefill/decode so decode is not stalled by prefill. The headline 127ms->23.1ms is ITL (P99), the inter-token latency, from the PR body's Scenario 2 test data (not TTFT; TTFT actually rises 160->227ms as the disagg tradeoff).

reported.scope: P99 inter-token latency of a disaggregated 1P1D (2xA800) serving run vs a single aggregated vLLM instance (1xA800); the gain comes from removing prefill-decode interference across two GPUs, not from an isolated op.
reported.scale_short: Author compares a 2-GPU disaggregated topology against a 1-GPU aggregated one. TO MAKE 1:1: stand up the full 1P1D xPyD proxy + two A800 instances and a matched single-instance baseline, then run the serving benchmark measuring ITL P99.
reported.scale_note: Multi-GPU disaggregated serving topology (proxy/router + P instance + D instance over NCCL); not reproducible on a single CPU/arm box. The 82% ITL drop is paid for by higher TTFT (160->227ms) and extra hardware (2x A800). Direction (lower ITL) is genuine for the disagg setup.
